title: Research whether using OBS Studio's Fullscreen Source Projector (a.k.a. fullscreen projector) to ...
objective: Research whether using OBS Studio's Fullscreen Source Projector (a.k.a. fullscreen projector) to feed a physical HDMI capture card in a TWO-PC streaming setup introduces any quality loss, latency, or efficiency problem versus the alternative of using Windows Display Duplication/extension feeding the capture card. Also assess whether the user's perceived concern that the PROJECTED feed's FPS appears to DECREASE over time in long sessions has any technical basis. Specifically: (1) Does the OBS fullscreen projector render at the source's native resolution with no recompression, i.e. is it effectively bit-perfect GPU output to the display output that the capture card then grabs? Does it add meaningful latency versus duplicating the display? Does it consume meaningful GPU and can it conflict with game rendering? (2) Known OBS issues across GitHub issues and obsproject.com forum threads: GPU downclocking during idle causing frame drops on projector windows, vsync timing of the projector window, memory leaks, dropped-frame reports, projector slowdown/performance regressions, whether borderless fullscreen window vs true fullscreen matters, and any documented 'frame rate drops after a while' reports related to fullscreen projector. (3) Is fullscreen projector considered the STANDARD best practice for feeding a capture card from a 2-monitor gaming PC so the gaming monitor can run higher res/refresh than the captured feed? Reference the Moonlight OBS capture-card guide, OBS forum threads, r/OBS. (4) Compare extending the Windows desktop to a 3rd display (with OBS projecting the source ONTO that 3rd display) versus duplicating Monitor 1. CONCLUDE: is the projector approach trustworthy for quality, is the 'FPS decreases over time' plausibly real and FIXABLE (how), and is it effectively the correct method? Give actionable advice. Cite source URLs with confidence.
